extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers, scholars, and students of philosophy/science interested in methodology of inquiry
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for structuring, practicing, and critiquing natural philosophy (scientific inquiry), including divisions of knowledge, proper roles for metaphysic/physic/mathematics, experiment design priorities, and organization of doubts and errors. Useful for assessing or producing methodological work in natural philosophy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division into speculative and operative parts
rubrics_metrics.description: Natural philosophy should be divided into two parts—the inquisition of causes (speculative, natural science) and the production of effects (operative, natural prudence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat these as distinct professions or occupations (pioneers who dig vs smiths who refine). Although connected, handle each severally; recognize a double ladder (ascending from experiments to causes and descending from causes to new experiments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of ancient terms with revised meanings
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep ancient philosophical terms where possible, but allow alteration of uses and definitions to serve truth and progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve antiquity 'usque ad aras' while clarifying and possibly redefining terms to avoid misunderstanding; do not invent new names unnecessarily as Aristotle did.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partition of natural science into physic and metaphysic
rubrics_metrics.description: Natural science/theory should be divided into physic (material and efficient causes; variable/respective causes) and metaphysic (formal and final causes; fixed/abstracted causes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand 'metaphysic' in a sense differing from received tradition: assign physic to the middle term between natural history and metaphysic; physic has three parts (configuration/universal, principles/originals, and particular variety).

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of physic: material and efficient causes
rubrics_metrics.description: Physic investigates material and efficient (respective/variable) causes and occupies a middle ground between natural history and metaphysic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physic's three parts: (1) configuration of things (de mundo), (2) principles/originals (seeds), (3) particular variety and qualities (as gloss on natural history). Do not neglect any of these parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metaphysic should seek forms (not gross substance-forms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Metaphysic should inquire into essential forms of qualities (sense, voluntary motion, vegetation, colours, gravity, etc.) rather than attempting to discover the full forms of complex substances (lion, oak).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat forms of basic qualities as an 'alphabet' that composes complex objects; avoid futile attempts to find forms of every composite substance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of metaphysic in unifying knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Metaphysic is valuable because it abridges the infinity of individual experience, unites notions, and supplies few simple forms whose combinations explain variety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rank knowledge by economy: the worthiest knowledge is that charged with least multiplicity (metaphysic). Knowledge of forms also enlarges freedom in operation and invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final causes must be confined to metaphysic (avoid mixing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inquiry into final causes is misplaced when mixed with physical inquiries; mixing final causes into physic has hindered discovery of real physical causes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep final causes within metaphysic to avoid 'remoras' that arrest investigation; recognize that final and physical causes can be compatible but should be treated in separate provinces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematics as a branch of metaphysic
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematics (quantity determined/proportionable) is best placed as a branch of metaphysic because it deals with essential, separable forms (figure, number).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish pure mathematics (geometry, arithmetic—quantity severed from natural axioms) and mixed mathematics (perspective, music, astronomy, architecture—auxiliary to natural philosophy). Value pure mathematics for sharpening the intellect and abstracting thought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division of natural prudence (operative) into three parts
rubrics_metrics.description: Natural prudence (operative natural philosophy) should be divided into experimental, philosophical, and magical parts, corresponding to natural history, physic, and metaphysic respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize experimental inventions found accidentally or by purposeful experiments; empiric inventions arise from varying/compounding experiments, philosophical inventions from knowledge of physical causes, and 'magical' (true natural magic) from knowledge of forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critique of degenerate natural magic (alchemy, astrology)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reject credulous, superstitious natural magic and degenerate arts where descriptions of means are more monstrous than the ends claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: True natural magic (operative freedom based on knowledge of forms) is legitimate but is currently deficient; distinguish plausible, laborious inquiry from vaporous imagination that produces chimeras.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create a calendar/inventory of inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Make an inventory (calendar) of all extant inventions (works of Nature or art) to note what is not yet invented and what comes nearest to seeming impossibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this calendar to awaken inquiry and deduce directions from speculation of causes; for each reputed impossibility, note the nearest extant thing to guide research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize experiments with universal consequence
rubrics_metrics.description: Value and prefer experiments that are of the most universal consequence and those that illuminate the invention of causes over experiments of only immediate or narrow use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An invention like the mariner’s needle (direction) can be as important as sails (motion); favor experiments that enable further invention and cause-discovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register doubts (calendars of problems) and resolve them
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain calendars of doubts (particular and total) to prevent premature assertion and to stimulate inquiry, but avoid keeping doubts permanently—work to resolve and then discard them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Doubts save philosophy from error and attract useful lines of work, but there is a danger that admitted doubts become permanent; encourage solving doubts rather than perpetuating uncertainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create a calendar of popular errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Compile a calendar of popular errors (especially in natural history) that persist in speech despite being demonstrably false.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document and convict such errors so that man's knowledge is not weakened by dross and vanity; use such a calendar to strengthen the foundation of knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Represent ancient philosophies whole and separately
rubrics_metrics.description: When collecting doctrines of ancient philosophers, report each philosophy in itself and not by packing together titles and fragments from many sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present the harmony of a philosophy internally (not bundled) to understand it properly; avoid fragmenting philosophies into topical bundles that make them appear foreign or monstrous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve continuity and entireness across partitions of knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat partitions of knowledge as veins, not separations; preserve continuity so particular sciences are nourished from the common fountain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid making disciplines barren by severing them (e.g., separating rhetoric from philosophy diminished rhetoric); allow cross-fertilization where appropriate (natural philosophy should inform medicine, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Human philosophy: study of self with two branches
rubrics_metrics.description: Human philosophy concerns knowledge of ourselves and divides into (a) discovery (how mind discloses through body) and (b) impression (how body affects mind and vice versa).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat this as an important part of natural philosophy, focusing on sympathies and concordances between mind and body which belong to neither purely bodily nor purely mental sciences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physiognomy and gestures (discovery branch)
rubrics_metrics.description: Study physiognomy (lineaments) and gestures (motions of countenance and parts) to discover the mind's disposition and present humour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize gestures as often more informative than static features; develop the art of reading motions and faces to detect dissimulation and guide business/interaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impression (interaction of body and mind)
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigate how bodily humours and states alter the mind, and conversely how passions and apprehensions of the mind alter the body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that this domain has been dispersed between medicine, religion, and superstition; collect and systematize knowledge (including therapeutic practices) while purging superstition.
